Co-parenting with a stranger

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We thought it was crazy when we started swiping right for love, but now people are using apps to find someone to have a baby with.

Summary:
Co-parenting with a stranger

We thought the world had gone mad when we started swiping right for love, but now people are swiping right to make babies. Apps like coparentmatch.com and being developed around the world to help strangers find sperm donors or even co-parent together.

Sebastian never wanted kids, he got married and the agreement was to travel the world and be child free. But, after a series of events, which included losing his brother in a motorcycle accident, Sebastian had a change of heart. His wife was 43 at the time and did not want to be pregnant or raise a child. Sebastian heard about co-parenting with a stranger from some of his gays friends and proposed the idea to his wife, who agreed.

His journey started on coparentmatch.com, where he met with around 20 women. After about 6 months of coffee dates with potential co-parents he hadn’t found anyone on the same page as him, about life. Then he got an email from a lesbian couple who asked if he would be a sperm donor, he said no, but he would be a dad. Together with his wife he met the couple for coffee, which turned into champagne and a year later, after getting to know each other, meeting with lawyers and psychologists, they went to the fertility clinic and made a baby

They used Sebastian’s sperm and Kristy’s eggs; she then carried the twins. They had a boy and a girl, who are now 4 years old. Sebastian’s marriage suffered a “COVID BREAKDOWN” but his journey as the twin’s father is what matters most to him now.
Him and “the girls”, as he calls them, co-parent on a 60-40 split, he picks the twins up twice a week after school and then takes them home for dinner, they also stay over at him on Fridays and every other holiday.
Sebastian pays for all school fees, extra murals, clothing, and a monthly maintenance, but legally if "the girls" decide to remove him from the family he has no legal right to the twins, as he is not on their birth certificate.


Further information:
We will spend 2 days living their lives and seeing exactly how co-parenting works
Shooting in scenes
• Family dinner outside on the grass/braai – couple and Sebastian about the reality of the decision they made
• Kids school drop off and pick-up
• Adult family meeting about schedules and planning the kids’ lives
• Sebastian and the girls at the park and the beach
• Moms and the girl’s bedtime routine
